relationship_review.rationale: Virgin Soil Epidemics already supports the existing environmental/global contributions; the queue flag was a shortened-title mismatch, not new relationship evidence.

The additions span the already represented Quebec, national and settler-colonial inquiries. CV metadata establishes books, articles and editorial credits; it does not establish new influence or a distinct ethnohistory claim without further reading.

The 1971 English collection includes earlier work, including the already dated ideology essay. Preserve the existing Marxist, language, cultural-studies and Thompson relationships; publication metadata alone adds no further intellectual relationship.

The added articles concern categories and sexual/racial regulation of colonial rule; existing postcolonial, gender, queer and anthropological contributions already provide those routes. The sovereignty article is metadata only, so no new sovereignty or political-theory argument is asserted.

Camera Lucida and Image-Music-Text extend the selected bibliography. Existing language/cultural-studies/philosophy relationships remain; neither translation date nor selection of earlier essays establishes an additional influence claim.
